note: Literature on biallelic NOTCH3 variants reports white matter hyperintensities involving the anterior temporal lobes and external capsule in some patients, though loss-of-function variants can show distinct or variable patterns.

evidence.text: A patient with a homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant presented with white matter abnormalities described as mainly involving the anterior temporal lobes and external capsules, reflecting a vascular leukoencephalopathy pattern.

source.title: A novel homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant in a Moroccan patient: expanding the spectrum beyond CADASIL
source.quote: mainly in anterior temporal lobes and external capsules; … , reflecting a vascular leukoencephalopathy pattern.

evidence.text: In a proband with a homozygous NOTCH3 null variant presenting with autosomal recessive early-onset leukoencephalopathy, MRI white matter abnormalities were observed without anterior temporal pole lesions.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: WES was performed on a proband who exhibited livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions.
